Tempe Brewery Tour: Your Complete Craft Beer Crawl Guide

Arizona's craft beer revolution has found a passionate home in Tempe. From the landmark Four Peaks Brewing Company to innovative newcomers, Tempe offers a diverse brewing scene worth exploring — and worth doing safely with professional transportation.

The short answer: a private brewery crawl is priced by the hour. The Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) at $175/hr covers a 4-stop, 4-hour Tempe tour for $700 before tax — about $44 per person with sixteen aboard. Couples take the Luxury SUV at $125/hr; big groups take the Party Bus (28 Pax) at $250/hr. Drinking on board is legal for passengers 21+ under A.R.S. § 4-251 — details below.

Tempe's Craft Beer Landscape

The Anchor: Four Peaks Brewing Company

Arizona's most famous craft brewery, Four Peaks has been a Tempe institution for decades. Located in a historic creamery building on 8th Street, it's where many Arizona beer lovers began their craft journey.

Must-Try: Kilt Lifter Scottish-Style Ale, Hop Knot IPA
Atmosphere: Historic, spacious, family-friendly during the day
Food: Full menu, beer-friendly fare

Planning Your Tempe Brewery Tour

Sample 4-Stop Tour (4-5 hours)

Stop 1: Four Peaks Brewing (8th Street)

  • Start with the classic
  • Historic setting, large-format bottles to share
  • 1-1.5 hours

Stop 2: the downtown Tempe rooftop brewery

  • Short ride to the downtown location
  • Rooftop if weather permits
  • 1 hour

Stop 3: Huss at Tempe Public Market

  • Experience the market vibe
  • Grab food from vendors
  • 1 hour

Stop 4: the South Tempe roadhouse

  • End with a casual Western atmosphere
  • Optional: late dinner
  • Flexible timing

Sample 6-Stop Tour (6-7 hours)

For serious craft beer enthusiasts, add:

  • Arizona Wilderness (Gilbert)
  • San Tan Brewing (Chandler)
  • Extended time at each location

Remember: a 7-hour booking earns one free hour, so a 7-hour tour bills 6 hours.

Tour Planning Tips

Timing Your Tour

Best Days:

  • Saturday afternoons (most breweries fully staffed)
  • Friday evenings (lively atmosphere)
  • Sunday afternoons (relaxed, often specials)

Avoid:

  • ASU football game days (traffic, crowds)
  • Major event weekends
  • Monday/Tuesday (some breweries closed or limited hours)

Eating Strategy

Option 1: Eat at a Brewery
Two of the four stops have full kitchens. Plan a meal stop.

Option 2: Food Before Touring
Grab lunch before starting, snack at breweries.

Option 3: Tempe Public Market
Multiple food vendors make this a great meal stop.

Important: Don't skip food. Craft beer on an empty stomach ends tours early.

Pace Management

Flight Strategy:
Order flights (4-5 small pours) rather than pints to sample more variety without overconsumption.

Water Matters:
We provide water in our vehicles. Drink between stops.

Know Your Limits:
A good brewery tour is about tasting and experiencing, not about volume.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can we bring our own beer in the vehicle?
A: Yes, if everyone drinking is 21 or older. Arizona's open-container law (A.R.S. § 4-251) exempts passengers in a vehicle for hire such as a party bus or limousine, so alcohol is legal on board. It's BYOB, nobody under 21 drinks, and the driver never does — read the full explainer. That said, we recommend saving your taste buds for the breweries.

Q: What if someone has too much?
A: We'll ensure they're safely transported. We may suggest cutting the tour short for everyone's comfort.

Q: Can you recommend breweries based on our tastes?
A: Absolutely. Tell us what you like — IPAs, stouts, sours, lagers — and we'll suggest stops.

Q: Do breweries require reservations?
A: Most don't for small groups. Large groups (10+) should call ahead.

Q: What about designated drivers?
A: That's why you hired us. Everyone can participate equally.
